newsitem.title: USA: U.S. adj retail sales up 2.8 pct in Feb - Redbook.
newsitem.headline: U.S. adj retail sales up 2.8 pct in Feb - Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 2.8 percent in the first two weeks of fiscal February versus January, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook Retail Sales Index.

The index rose 6.1 percent compared with the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales advanced 6.5 percent in the week ended February 15 compared with the same week a year ago, it said.
Howard Eilenberg, a retail analyst at Lynch, Jones & Ryan, said the sustained swift pace of sales growth in February is somewhat unexpected.
"We're pleasantly surprised by what we're seeing," Eilenberg said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television. "Primarily, it's the good economic climate," he added.
Retail's strength appears to be broadly based, with particularly solid performance in the western United States, Eilenberg said.
Looking ahead, February probably will lose some steam in its final weeks but an early Easter should boost March figures, he said.
